text:
evan-marketing: Hey @rosa-runtime and @kevin-eng — small but important ask for next week's launch post and the webinar. Can runtime produce a tiny reproducibility / proof pack we can link in the blog and hand to press?

rosa-runtime: Sure. What do you want in the proof pack?

evan-marketing: Minimal and verifiable: 4 canonical payloads (micro, short, mid, tail), timings CSV with p50/p95/p99, one cold-start trace, one steady-state trace, a one-paragraph run-note describing warmup and batching, and a 2-line press blurb with exact numbers we can quote. Also a tiny demo snippet for the laptop team.

kevin-eng: Which model + infra should we run on? Demo model or the launch variant?

evan-marketing: Please run the demo model (rwd-mini-2b) on dedicated-gpu-18 so numbers are stable. If that machine's busy, run hosted and call out caveats. Sequence distro we want mirrored in the README: 50% <=64, 30% 65-512, 20% 513-2048.

rosa-runtime: Plan: micro-sweep 600 requests, batching off, 50 warmup, collect tokens/sec and latencies. Will produce timings.csv, payloads.csv (with seq lengths), traces.tar (cold + steady), provenance.txt (instance id, driver, docker tag), and demo/run-local.sh. ETA ~20h.

demo-sre: Can you include a copy-pasteable curl and an env var example for the demo laptop? We need zero-friction commands.

rosa-runtime: Yep. Example to include: ```bash
export RW_KEY=<KEY>
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" -d '{"model":"rwd-mini-2b","input":"Explain blockchain in two sentences"}'
```

evan-marketing: Nice. Important: if int8 quantized run is included, mark it clearly as 'experimental' or 'preliminary' if variance >10% vs fp16 and include raw traces. We must avoid overclaiming.

kevin-eng: Agreed. We'll run fp16 baseline and int8 quick-check. If int8 stddev at p95 > 12% we'll label as noisy and still include raw CSVs.

rosa-runtime: Also adding a tiny README.md summarizing the run: job id, date, model, infra, batching policy, warmup count, sample distribution, and the exact commands used. Will include request counts per bucket so marketing can compute weighted averages.

benchbot: micro-bench job queued (#81007) by rosa-runtime. Logs: /bench/81007. ETA ~2h.

evan-marketing: Topline ask for the press blurb: a single sentence like "Measured on rwd-mini-2b (dedicated-gpu-18), p95 = XX ms over 600 requests" — we'll craft wording but need the raw number.

rosa-runtime: I'll include press_blurb.txt with the raw numbers and the provenance line. Example provenance: "Measured on rwd-mini-2b, dedicated-gpu-18 (ami-2026.04, nvidia-driver=545.65, docker:redwood/runtime:2.4.1), p95 computed over 600 requests, batching disabled."

kevin-eng: Minor request  include the sequence length histogram (counts) and a tiny column in timings.csv for sequence_length so you can filter later.

rosa-runtime: Good call. Will add sequence_length column and include payloads.csv mapping example->expected tokens_out for the demo.

demo-sre: Also add a one-liner about environmental noise: "no other noisy tenants on the machine during the run" or note if shared. Helps press know the run context.

rosa-runtime: Will state that explicitly in provenance.txt. If hosted run used, I'll list rate limits and concurrency used.

benchbot: micro-bench #81007 completed. Artifacts uploaded to /bench/81007/artifacts.tar.gz (sha256: 7c9f1a4b...).

evan-marketing: Amazing, thank you. If any of the artifacts look noisy or the long payload causes time blowup, flag us early and we'll drop the long sample so you can ship the pack. :raised_hands:
